title: IBM Releases Qiskit SDK v2.6 with C API Pass-Manager Framework, Native QPY Serialization, and Custom Operations - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM Quantum released Qiskit SDK v2.6, expanding its C API with a QkPassManager compiler-pass framework, native QPY serialization (QPY v18 now default) and custom operations via a C vtable, so compilation can run from C, C++ and Julia without Python. The updated roadmap has v2.7 declaring C ABI/API stability and adding a Medium IR for fault-tolerant instruction sets, and v2.8 deploying the Rust-native BackendV3.

insights.claim: IBM Quantum's Qiskit SDK v2.6 expands Qiskit's C API layer so essential compilation capabilities run in native C, C++ and Julia environments without requiring a Python runtime.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Python-optional Qiskit makes IBM's stack easier to embed in HPC centers, reinforcing Qiskit as the default quantum SDK.
insights.quote: bringing essential compilation capabilities to native C, C++, and Julia environments without requiring a Python runtime

insights.claim: Qiskit v2.6 adds QkPassManager, a generic C API pass-manager framework in which passes declare input and output representations via QkIrHandle descriptors and the manager validates the full pipeline before execution, enabling multi-stage lowering for C, C++, Julia and Fortran.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lets third parties build custom compiler passes natively, deepening the Qiskit ecosystem.
insights.locator: The new pass-manager framework extends Qiskit

insights.claim: Qiskit v2.6 exposes native binary QPY serialization directly to C and lets users define custom hardware-native quantum operations through a C vtable interface (QkCustomOp) without Python object model overhead.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware vendors can plug native gates into Qiskit cheaply, widening its reach beyond IBM hardware.
insights.locator: Qiskit v2.6 introduces a generic C

insights.claim: QPY format v18 becomes the default serialization in Qiskit v2.6, with more compact encoding of quantum and classical registers that reduces file sizes for large circuits while staying compatible with Python's qiskit.qpy module.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Incremental tooling efficiency for large-scale circuit workflows.
insights.locator: The update also makes QPY format

insights.claim: Building Qiskit from source now requires Rust 1.89, the minimum runtime remains Python 3.10, and Python 3.11+ will be required starting in Qiskit v2.7.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Operational note for teams maintaining Qiskit-based pipelines.
insights.locator: The update also makes QPY format

insights.claim: The Qiskit v2.6 C API enhancements advance IBM's roadmap toward Python-optional execution within tightly coupled HPC and Quantum-Centric Supercomputing architectures, including initial removal of the libpython linker dependency from the core libqiskit library.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM is positioning Qiskit as infrastructure inside supercomputers, a bid to own the HPC-quantum integration layer.

themes.theme: Qiskit roadmap to Rust core and fault tolerance

insights.claim: Qiskit 2.7, in development, will formally declare ABI and API stability guarantees for the C interface and introduce a Medium Intermediate Representation (MIR) to support compilation to fault-tolerant instruction sets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Fault-tolerant compilation support in the SDK tracks IBM's move toward error-corrected hardware.

insights.claim: Qiskit 2.8, planned, will deploy BackendV3, a Rust-native execution interface exposed to Python and C/C++, and integrate the Samplomatic library into Qiskit's quantum program datamodel.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A Rust-native backend interface may reshape how hardware providers integrate with Qiskit.
